paragraphs.text: Let W be a set of alternatives, q:W→Q the requested answer, and τ_A:W→T_A and τ_B:W→T_B two declared traces. For any map f, write K(f) for its kernel relation: two alternatives are related when f gives them the same value. Let f[W] be the reachable image. Here a finite abstraction means that its reachable trace image is finite; W itself need not be finite.
Exact certification. Cert(q | f) holds when a decoder d:f[W]→Q exists with q=d∘f on W. Restricting d to the reachable image avoids silently assigning answers to impossible traces.

The fiber-factorization criterion says that exact certification holds if and only if every f-fiber is q-constant, equivalently K(f)⊆K(q) (Pang 2026a). Form the joint trace τ=<τ_A,τ_B> and its reachable image R=τ[W]⊆T_A×T_B. Then:

This is the common refinement of the two fiber partitions, a standard construction in the theory of equivalence relations (Ore 1942). In epistemic language it has the same shape as distributed knowledge: the group can eliminate possibilities that no member eliminates alone (Halpern and Moses 1990). The formulation is task-relative. It says nothing by itself about causation, cooperation, or physical interaction.

Definition. The pair has strict exact synergy for q when the joint trace certifies q but neither individual trace does. Equivalently, each trace has at least one q-conflicting collision, but no q-conflicting pair is collapsed by both.

The canonical finite example is XOR. Take W={0,1}², τ_A(x,y)=x, τ_B(x,y)=y, and q(x,y)=x XOR y. Each single-coordinate fiber contains both q-values, so neither trace certifies q. The pair recovers (x,y), and the decoder computes XOR. The effect is fiber alignment, not raw capacity: each individual trace already has as many labels as q has answers. Williams and Beer use the same XOR pattern as a canonical example of information available only jointly, although numerical partial-information decompositions require additional choices (Williams and Beer 2010).

First boundary. Individual insufficiency never proves joint insufficiency. To block the pair, one needs a target-conflicting collision shared by both traces, or a separately justified capacity obstruction.

If the reachable images of τ_A and τ_B have m_A and m_B values, then |R|≤m_A m_B. Joint certification therefore requires |q[W]|≤|R|≤m_A m_B. The inequality is necessary, not sufficient; the kernel condition decides whether the labels fall on the right fibers. This is a fixed-interface statement. Variable-length records, growing memories, fresh observations, or families indexed by input size are different interfaces and need their own uniform analysis.
